subject.title: fix(agents): xAI/Grok requests fail after a stale reasoning replay ("could not decrypt encrypted_content")

question: Should maintainers accept the pre-fix production logs plus positive/negative predicate tests as sufficient evidence for this non-inducible xAI rotation error, or keep waiting for an organic after-fix Grok run?
rationale: The contributor explains that the exact code-less xAI decrypt error only occurs after provider-side snapshot/key rotation, so normal synthetic proof would exercise a different coded error path.

options.title: Accept proof limitation
options.body: Treat the production pre-fix logs, existing one-shot retry behavior, and focused positive/negative unit coverage as enough for this narrow P1 recovery fix, then refresh exact-head CI before merge.

options.title: Wait for organic after-fix logs
options.body: Keep the proof gate until a future xAI rotation produces redacted gateway logs showing the retry succeeds after this branch.

options.title: Request alternate maintainer proof
options.body: Ask for a maintainer-run gateway replay that exercises the new predicate without claiming to reproduce xAI's provider-side rotation.

recommendation.title: Accept proof limitation
recommendation.body: Treat the production pre-fix logs, existing one-shot retry behavior, and focused positive/negative unit coverage as enough for this narrow P1 recovery fix, then refresh exact-head CI before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Closest current history owner for the same encrypted-content retry predicate and adjacent merged recovery behavior.
